meta.title: Japan 2027
meta.about: Solo ski trip. Confirmed: JQ815 BNE→SYD and the Business Classic Reward SYD→MEL→NRT on 8 Feb. Home Tue 16 Feb on QF80 + QF1256 (booked). Everything else is planned from research done 13 Sep 2026; prices marked est. need checking when booking.

days.title: Fly out via Sydney and Melbourne
days.notes: Times on this day are shown in local time at each airport. Sydney and Melbourne are one hour ahead of Queensland in February (daylight saving).

items.title: Drive Gympie → Brisbane Airport
items.notes: Book AIRPARK online beforehand (free shuttle every 10-15 min to the domestic terminal). Leaving at 6 puts you at the terminal by ~8:00. Jetstar check-in opens 2 h before and bag drop closes 40 min before departure (9:05), so 8:00-8:15 is the target.

items.title: JQ815 Brisbane → Sydney (booked, Classic Reward)
items.notes: Jetstar, economy Classic Reward. Departs 9:45 Queensland time, lands 12:20 Sydney time (Sydney is an hour ahead in February). Six hours of buffer before QF481. Bags are NOT checked through to Narita on Jetstar: you collect them in Sydney. Reward bookings include a 20 kg bag but the confirmation sometimes shows 0 kg; check it.

items.title: Collect bag, walk T2 → T3, re-check bag with Qantas for QF481
items.location: Sydney T2 baggage hall → covered walkway (7 min) → T3 Qantas bag drop
items.notes: Qantas accepts domestic bags from about 6 hours before departure, so from 12:30 you are fine. Check in for QF481 online the day before (24 h out) so you only need the bag drop. Then security and up to the lounge. If the bag drop refuses the bag early, wait landside at the T3 cafes until it opens; the lounge is airside.

items.title: Qantas Domestic Business Lounge, Sydney T3
items.location: Opposite gates 4-5, up the escalator, left door
items.notes: Your Business ticket (QF481 boarding pass) gets you in. Five hours: shower, eat lightly (the Melbourne First Lounge dinner is better), charge everything, download offline maps.

items.title: QF481 Sydney → Melbourne
items.notes: Business, A321neo, 1h35. Confirmed.

items.title: Melbourne T1 → T2 walk, then immigration
items.location: Covered walkway, one level up, 3-5 min
items.notes: Bags transfer automatically on the one booking. Allow 30-40 min for security and outbound immigration.

items.title: Qantas International First Lounge, Melbourne T2 (Titanium pass)
items.notes: Use one of your two Titanium First Lounge invitations here (show it in the Qantas app). Proper restaurant dining, so skip the Sydney lounge food and eat here. Be at the gate by ~10:45pm. Fallback if anything goes wrong with the pass: the International Business Lounge on level 1 is covered by the ticket.

items.title: QF49 Melbourne → Tokyo Narita
items.notes: Business, A330-200, 10h20, lands 7:50am Tuesday. Sleep as much as you can: Japan is only 1 hour behind Queensland, so jet lag is minimal.

days.title: Land, straight down to Osaka
days.notes: Long travel day on purpose: it puts you in Osaka the night before the calmest weekday to do Universal Studios.

items.title: Land Narita T2, immigration and customs
items.notes: Have the Visit Japan Web QR code ready (immigration + customs in one). Budget about an hour. Pick up your bag, switch on the eSIM, and withdraw ¥30,000-40,000 at the 7-Eleven ATM in the terminal (Nozawa is largely cash-only and has one foreign-card ATM, at the post office). Suica: Welcome Suica Mobile in Apple Wallet if you have an iPhone; on Android buy a physical Welcome Suica at the JR counter.

items.title: Narita Express → Tokyo Station
items.notes: ~55 min. Buy at the JR East ticket office or machine (the N’EX round-trip ticket for foreign passports, ¥5,200, is worth it because you come back this way on the 15th).

items.title: Ekiben (station bento) from Ekibenya Matsuri
items.notes: The most Japanese lunch there is. Grab one for the Shinkansen. Not a trendy place, just a shop with 200 regional bento.

items.title: Nozomi Shinkansen Tokyo → Shin-Osaka
items.notes: ~2h30, every 10 min. Reserve a seat (opens one month ahead on smart-EX). A normal suitcase under 160 cm total is fine; only bags over 160 cm need the oversized-baggage seat.

items.title: Shin-Osaka → hotel
items.location: JR local to Osaka / Fukushima, or Yumesaki line to Universal City

items.title: Check in, Osaka (2 nights)
items.notes: Solo, private room. Business hotels around Fukushima or Tenma are quiet, cheap and 15-25 min from USJ by train.

items.title: Send the suitcase ahead by Yamato courier (takkyubin)
items.notes: Ask the desk for “takkyubin to this address” and show the destination’s name and address in Japanese. Plan A: to the Nozawa lodging, waiting when you arrive Thursday. Plan B: to the Takayama hub hotel (write “for guest arriving 12 Feb”; hotels hold parcels). Two days is the standard lead time. Travel in between with a daypack: two or three days of clothes, USJ tickets, and in Plan A Friday’s ski base layers. Confirm beforehand that the receiving place accepts parcels (most do).

items.title: Nintendo OSAKA store (optional, 45 min)
items.location: Daimaru Umeda 13F, 5 min walk from JR Osaka Station
items.notes: The official Nintendo store, exclusive merchandise, quieter than the USJ shops on Wednesday. Open 10:00-20:00. Borrowed from your friend’s Tokyo list (theirs was the Shibuya Parco store).

items.title: Walk Nakazakicho and Tenma
items.location: Nakazakicho (old wooden lanes) → Tenjinbashisuji shopping arcade → Tenma
items.notes: Low-key neighbourhoods a short train ride from Umeda. Tenjinbashisuji is 2.6 km of covered arcade where locals shop.

items.title: Dinner in the Tenma izakaya alleys
items.location: Around Tenma station, under the tracks
items.notes: Standing bars and tiny izakaya, mostly Japanese customers. Order doteyaki (beef tendon simmered in miso) and kushikatsu. Early night; tomorrow starts at 7.

days.title: Universal Studios Japan and Super Nintendo World
days.notes: Wednesday is the calmest weekday in the window (Thursday is a public holiday, and the weekend follows). Buy the Studio Pass and an Express Pass that includes Super Nintendo World entry as soon as they go on sale for this date.

items.title: Train to Universal City
items.location: Osaka Station platform 1 → Universal City (JR Yumesaki line, ~12 min direct)

items.title: Be at the gates before official opening
items.notes: Posted opening is usually 9:00-9:30 in February but the park regularly opens 30-60 min early. Being there by 7:45 matters if you are relying on the free timed-entry ticket. Log into the USJ app the night before and make sure the eSIM has data: the timed-entry ticket is app-only (since Jan 2026) and needs signal at the gate.

items.title: Enter USJ; claim Super Nintendo World timed entry in the app the second you are through the gate
items.notes: 1-Day Studio Pass, date-priced (¥8,900 low season up to ¥11,800 peak in 2026; Feb 2027 not published yet). If you bought an Express Pass with area entry you already have a slot and can skip the scramble.

items.title: Super Nintendo World: Mario Kart, Yoshi’s Adventure, Donkey Kong Country
items.notes: The ¥4,800 is the Power-Up Band (optional but it is the whole point of the key challenges and Bowser Jr boss fight). Ride Mario Kart first, then Donkey Kong’s Mine Cart, then wander.

items.title: Kinopio’s Cafe (Toad’s cafe)
items.notes: Reserve in the app on the day if slots show. Otherwise Yoshi’s Snack Island for a quick bite.

items.title: Rest of the park: Jurassic Park, Harry Potter area, Jaws
items.notes: Single Rider lines are the solo traveller’s cheat code and are free. February weekdays historically close around 7pm, so the day is shorter than summer: front-load Nintendo World.

items.title: Okonomiyaki dinner back in town
items.location: A neighbourhood okonomiyaki counter near the hotel (see Food)

culture.title: Universal Studios Japan and Super Nintendo World
culture.notes: The one early-ish start in this plan, and only if you want it: without an Express Pass the free Super Nintendo World timed-entry ticket is gone minutes after opening, so the 7:00 train matters. With an Express Pass that includes area entry (recommended, ~¥12,800) you can take the 8:30 train, be at the gate by 9:15 and lose nothing. Buy the pass when the date opens (~12 Dec) and sleep in.

days.title: Osaka → Narai-juku (Edo post town) → Nozawa Onsen
days.notes: National Foundation Day, so reserve every seat a month ahead. The Shinano express runs straight through the Kiso valley, so this is the day to see rural Japan for free: hop off at Kiso-Fukushima, ride one local stop to Narai-juku, walk the 1 km Edo-period street in the snow, then carry on to Nagano. Travel hands-free: the suitcase goes ahead by courier from Osaka (see Tuesday).

items.title: Check out (daypack only), to Shin-Osaka
Nozomi Shin-Osaka → Nagoya
items.notes: ~50 min, reserved seat.

items.title: Limited Express Shinano Nagoya → Kiso-Fukushima
items.notes: Reserved seat on the holiday. Sit on the left for the Kiso river. Buy the ticket through to Nagano with a break at Kiso-Fukushima, or two tickets; either is fine.

items.title: Local train Kiso-Fukushima → Narai
items.location: Kiso-Fukushima, Chuo line local (about every hour)
items.notes: 20 minutes. Check the local timetable when you reserve the Shinano so the connection is short.

items.title: Narai-juku: the best-preserved post town on the old Nakasendo road
items.location: Narai station → 1 km of Edo-period wooden inns and shops
items.notes: A working village, not a theme park: lacquerware workshops, a sake shop, temples up the side lanes, snow on the eaves. Narai station has no lockers but a ¥300 bag-minding desk (8:30-16:00) if you are carrying anything. Lunch here: soba or gohei-mochi (grilled rice cake with walnut-miso), the Kiso valley specialty. The Kiso Ohashi bridge and Kamidonya museum are worth 20 minutes.

items.title: Gohei-mochi and Kiso soba in Narai
items.location: Any shop on the main street with a menu outside

items.title: Local train Narai → Shiojiri, then Shinano Shiojiri → Nagano
items.notes: Local 25 min to Shiojiri, change to the Shinano (about hourly) for ~65 min to Nagano. Reserve the Shiojiri → Nagano seat too.

items.title: Hokuriku Shinkansen Nagano → Iiyama
items.notes: 12 minutes. The Nozawa Onsen Liner leaves about 10 min after each Shinkansen.

items.title: Nozawa Onsen Liner → Nozawa Onsen
items.location: Iiyama Station, bus stop out the front
items.notes: 25 min. Taxi is the fallback (¥6,000-7,000). Tell the lodging you arrive about 6pm so dinner is held.

items.title: Check in, Nozawa Onsen (5 nights)
items.location: See Stays for the shortlist and how to book
items.notes: Your suitcase should be waiting (sent by courier on Tuesday). If it is not, the daypack has tomorrow’s ski layers.

items.title: Ryokan dinner (or Wakagiri if no meals booked)
items.notes: Ryokan dinners are served at a fixed time; say so at check-in. If you are eating out, Wakagiri is the local favourite for a home-style set meal.

items.title: Oyu, the main public bathhouse
items.notes: 13 free soto-yu bathhouses run by the village. Wash first, no towel in the water, keep it quiet, no photos. Bring a small towel; expect it hot.

items.title: Check out (daypack only), subway to Namba
Nankai to Gokurakubashi, cable car, bus into town
items.location: Nankai Namba → Gokurakubashi (Limited Express Koya ~80 min, or express with a change at Hashimoto ~100 min) → cable car 5 min → bus 10 min to Senjuinbashi
items.notes: Buy the Koyasan World Heritage Ticket at Namba (~¥3,980): return train, cable car and unlimited Koyasan buses for two days. Reserve the limited express seat for the holiday.

items.title: Lunch near Senjuinbashi: soba, udon or a shojin set
Danjo Garan (the great pagoda) and Kongobuji head temple
items.notes: Kongobuji has the largest rock garden in Japan and painted sliding doors; Konpon Daito is the vermilion pagoda. Bus or 15 min walk between them.

items.title: Check in at the shukubo (temple lodging)
items.location: See Stays: Ekoin, Fukuchiin or Shojoshin-in
items.notes: Tatami room, shared baths, dinner served in your room by monks-in-training. Curfew around 9pm. Solo guests are normal here.

items.title: Okunoin cemetery walk to Kobo Daishi’s mausoleum
items.notes: 200,000 graves under thousand-year cedars, lanterns, snow. The single most atmospheric walk in Japan. Photography stops at the last bridge; go quiet there.

items.title: Shojin ryori dinner at the temple
items.notes: Vegetarian Buddhist cuisine: sesame tofu (goma-dofu, the Koyasan speciality), mountain vegetables, tempura. Included in the lodging price.

items.title: Okunoin night tour with a monk (optional)
items.notes: Ekoin runs an English-language night walk most evenings; other temples can book you on it.

culture.title: Osaka → Koyasan (temple lodging)
culture.notes: National Foundation Day. Koyasan is a 1,200-year-old monastery town on a forested plateau, two hours from Namba: 117 temples, a 2 km cemetery walk through giant cedars, and a night in a temple with the monks’ vegetarian dinner. Late-morning start; the suitcase went ahead to the Takayama hub on Tuesday, so this is daypack only.

days.title: Ski Nozawa, day 1
days.notes: Thursday was a stand-alone public holiday, so Friday is the comparatively quiet day before the weekend crowd arrives. Be on the Nagasaka gondola at opening (8:30) and head to Yamabiko at the top.

items.title: Ski rental fitting (pre-booked, 4 days)
items.notes: 4 days x ¥4,450 standard set (skis, boots, poles) at a village shop; the resort shop is ¥5,500/day. Book online in January with your boot size in cm: big sizes (29 cm+) run out in peak weeks. Ski wear can be rented too.

items.title: Nozawa Onsen Snow Resort, full day
items.notes: Special Pack: 1-day lift pass + ¥1,000 lunch voucher (2025-26 price; expect +5-10%). 297 ha, 1,085 m vertical, 10 km longest run (Skyline). Yamabiko for tree runs, Uenotaira for cruising.

items.title: Lunch on the mountain with the voucher
items.notes: Curry rice or ramen; the voucher covers most of it.

items.title: Onsen: try a different soto-yu (Kuma no Tearai or Shinyu)
Soba at Sobadokoro Daimon
items.notes: Hand-cut Shinshu soba. Order it zaru (cold) even in winter; it is how locals judge a soba shop.

items.title: Morning prayers and the goma fire ritual (optional)
items.notes: Worth it once in a lifetime, but nobody checks. Breakfast is served around 7:30 regardless.

items.title: Temple breakfast in your room
Bus, cable car and Nankai back to Namba, subway to Shin-Osaka
items.notes: Return leg is covered by the World Heritage Ticket; the subway hop is ¥300.

items.title: Nozomi Shin-Osaka → Nagoya
Kishimen noodles on the Nagoya platform
items.notes: Five-minute stand-up lunch, the Nagoya thing.

items.title: Limited Express Hida Nagoya → Takayama
items.notes: ~2h30 up the Hida river gorge; reserved seat. Hida trains run about hourly, so the exact one depends on the connection.

items.title: Check in to the hub, Takayama (4 nights); the suitcase is waiting
items.notes: Unpack. This room is home until Tuesday; Saturday night you simply do not sleep in it.

items.title: Evening free
items.notes: Sanmachi old town is 10 minutes away: sake breweries with cedar balls outside (tastings for a few hundred yen), the river, Hida beef whenever you are hungry.

items.title: Hida beef dinner (whenever, wherever)
items.location: A local grill or hoba-miso restaurant off the main drag
items.notes: Hida beef on a magnolia leaf with miso is the dish. Skip the ones with touts.

culture.title: Koyasan → Takayama, the hub for four nights
culture.notes: The 6:30 prayers are optional; breakfast is at a fixed time around 7:30, then a leisurely trip: down the mountain, Shinkansen to Nagoya, the Hida express up the gorge. Check into one room for four nights and unpack properly. Evening free.

days.title: Ski Nozawa, day 2
days.notes: Saturday of the long weekend: busy, so early start. Karasawa and Paradise are quieter than the gondola-top runs. Night skiing on Hikage runs on selected nights; check the board. Rental gear is easiest to fit first thing Friday, so plan on being at the shop when it opens.

items.title: Nozawa Onsen Snow Resort, full day
items.notes: Special Pack again. Explore Karasawa and Paradise; the Skyline run top to bottom late afternoon when it empties.

items.title: Mountain lunch
Onsen eggs at the Ogama
items.location: Ogama (the village’s boiling cooking spring, locals only in the water but you can watch and buy eggs nearby)

items.title: Izakaya dinner: basashi (horse sashimi) and nozawana
Miyagawa morning market (runs until noon)
items.notes: Farmers, pickles, mitarashi dango (soy-glazed rice dumplings) for a second breakfast.

items.title: Nohi bus Takayama → Shirakawa-go
items.location: Takayama Nohi Bus Center (next to the station)
items.notes: 50 min. Reserve the seat; reserved services sell out on weekends. Daypack only; the suitcase stays in the hub room.

items.title: Lunch: soba or a Hida beef croquette from a stand
Shirakawa-go: Shiroyama viewpoint, Wada House, the walk between the farmhouses
items.notes: Viewpoint shuttle or a 20 min walk up. Wada House (¥400) is the big one you can go inside. Snow boots and crampons: the paths are icy.

items.title: Check in at a gassho-zukuri farmhouse minshuku
items.location: See Stays; book via the Shirakawa-go Tourist Association site
items.notes: Day-trippers leave on the last buses around 5; then the village is yours. Dinner is around the irori hearth with the family.

items.title: Blue hour in the empty village; Shirakawa-go no Yu onsen (optional)
Irori hearth dinner at the farmhouse
items.notes: Grilled river fish, mountain vegetables, local tofu, included in the price.

culture.title: Shirakawa-go farmhouse night (night out no. 2)
culture.notes: Leave the suitcase in the Takayama room and go with a daypack. Shirakawa-go’s thatched farmhouses under two metres of snow are the picture everyone has of rural Japan; it is busy from 10 to 3, and sleeping in one of the houses means you get it at dusk and dawn. Late-morning bus; no light-up event in Feb 2027.

days.title: Rural day: Togakushi shrine in the snow, then Zenko-ji
days.notes: Sunday is the most crowded ski day of the trip (long-weekend Tokyo crowd), so it is the cheapest day to give up. Togakushi is a mountain shrine village above Nagano: a 2 km avenue of 400-year-old cedars leading to the inner shrine, all under deep snow in February, plus the soba the village is famous for. Back via Zenko-ji, one of Japan’s great temples. If it is dumping powder on Sunday morning, swap this for skiing and call the day a rest instead; the ski item below is kept as the alternative.

items.title: Nozawa Onsen Liner → Iiyama, Shinkansen → Nagano
items.notes: Check the Liner and Shinkansen times the night before; Sunday services are the same as weekdays.

items.title: Alpico bus 70 Nagano Station → Togakushi
items.location: Nagano Station east side, bus stop 7
items.notes: About 60 min to Chusha (middle shrine). In winter a separate winter service stops at the Okusha entrance; if the bus you are on does not, get off at Chusha and walk up the road ~30 min or take a taxi. The Zenko-ji & Togakushi 1-day bus ticket (Alpico) covers the whole day’s buses and is cheaper than singles.

items.title: Okusha cedar avenue and inner shrine
items.notes: 20 min flat walk through the cedars to the red Zuishinmon gate, then a steeper 20-30 min to the inner shrine, all on packed snow. Bring or buy simple crampons (Workman or Don Quijote sell them for ~¥1,500) and waterproof boots; ski gloves and shell are perfect. Quiet, no ropes, no gates: this is the rural Japan you asked for.

items.title: Togakushi soba at Chusha
items.location: Around Chusha (middle shrine): Uzuraya is the famous one, several quieter shops nearby
items.notes: Togakushi soba is served in small “bocchi” bundles on a bamboo tray. Order zaru, add the local wasabi. Cash.

items.title: Chusha shrine and the ninja museum village (optional)
items.notes: Chusha has an 800-year-old triple cedar at its gate. Skip the ninja stuff unless it amuses you.

items.title: Bus 70 Togakushi → Zenko-ji (Daimon stop)
items.notes: Get off at Zenkoji Daimon, not the station. Last buses back down are around 17:00-18:00; check the winter timetable.

items.title: Zenko-ji temple at dusk
items.notes: 1,400-year-old temple, the reason Nagano exists. Walk the main hall, do the pitch-black “kaidan meguri” tunnel under the altar to touch the key to paradise (¥600). The approach street (Nakamise) has oyaki and miso shops.

items.title: Nagano → Iiyama → Nozawa Onsen
items.location: Nagano Station (15 min walk or bus from Zenko-ji)

items.title: Last Nozawa dinner: oyaki, nozawana and a nabe hotpot
Pack; return rental gear tonight if the shop allows, or first thing tomorrow
ALTERNATIVE if it is a powder day: ski Nozawa instead
items.notes: Marked as skipped so it stays out of the budget. Flip the status to Planned and set the Togakushi items to Skipped if you choose to ski. Sunday lift lines ease after 2pm.

items.title: Breakfast at the hearth, then a slow walk while the village is still empty
items.notes: Farmhouse breakfast is at a set time, usually 7:30-8:00. The walk after it is optional.

items.title: Nohi bus Shirakawa-go → Takayama
Takayama ramen
items.location: An old shop in the centre
items.notes: Thin curly noodles in a soy-shoyu broth; the town’s everyday lunch.

items.title: Free afternoon
items.notes: Option: Hida Furukawa, 15 minutes by train, a small canal town with carp, white storehouses and two sake breweries, almost no tourists. Or the hotel bath and a nap.

items.title: Dinner: hoba-miso set or an izakaya near the station

culture.title: Back to the hub, free afternoon
culture.notes: Sleep in, breakfast at the hearth, a late-morning bus back. The afternoon is open: the quiet canal town of Hida Furukawa is 15 minutes by train, or do nothing at all.

days.title: Ski Nozawa, day 3 (the quiet Monday)
days.notes: The long-weekend crowd went home last night. This is the emptiest the mountain will be all trip, which is exactly why the trip now ends Tuesday.

items.title: Nozawa Onsen Snow Resort, full day
items.notes: Special Pack again. Skyline top to bottom with nobody on it; Yamabiko trees if it snowed overnight.

items.title: Mountain lunch
Onsen, then pack most of the bag
Last Nozawa dinner: basashi, nozawana, a nabe hotpot
Confirm tomorrow: Liner time, Shinkansen reservation, rental return, cash to settle the bill
Free-roam day; the options are all optional
items.notes: Nothing booked, nothing before 9:30.

items.title: Option: Okuhida onsen villages (Hirayu Onsen, 1 h by bus)
items.location: Nohi bus from Takayama Bus Center
items.notes: Open-air hot spring baths in the snow (Hirayu no Mori, ¥700), and the Shinhotaka Ropeway another 40 min on for a snow panorama of the Northern Alps. Back by dinner. About ¥5,000 in buses and baths.

items.title: Option: Gero Onsen (1 h by train)
items.notes: One of Japan’s “three great onsen”; a bathhouse pass (Yumeguri Tegata, ¥1,500) gets you into three of the ryokan baths. Riverside foot baths are free.

items.title: Option: Takayama Jinya, Hida Folk Village, the Higashiyama temple walk
items.notes: The only surviving Edo provincial government office (¥440); a hillside of relocated farmhouses (¥700); a quiet 3.5 km walk past a dozen temples above town.

items.title: Last Takayama dinner: Hida beef properly, or sushi at a counter

culture.title: Free-roam day from the hub
culture.notes: Deliberately empty. The options below are all easy from Takayama station and none starts before 9:30. Pick one, or none.

days.title: Morning ski, then home via Tokyo
days.notes: QF80 is booked for 19:20, so the noon bus out of Nozawa is the latest sensible one.

items.title: Short morning ski (optional)
items.notes: Only if the lodging allows a late checkout and the rental shop opens early. Otherwise a slow breakfast and one last bathhouse.

items.title: Return rental gear, check out, settle in cash
Nozawa Onsen Liner → Iiyama Station
Hokuriku Shinkansen Iiyama → Tokyo
items.notes: ~1h50, reserve the seat (Hakutaka services stop at Iiyama roughly hourly).

items.title: Narita Express Tokyo → Narita T2
items.notes: Covered by the N’EX round trip ticket bought on day 1 (valid 14 days).

items.title: Narita T2: check in, drop bag, tax-free refund counter if you shopped
items.notes: QF80 check-in closes 18:20. Check in online 24 h before and pick a seat.

items.title: Dinner at Narita T2 food court
items.notes: Tonkatsu or ramen; last Japanese meal.

items.title: QF80 Narita → Melbourne
items.notes: Confirmed. Overnight A330, 10h25, Economy Sale fare. Try adding Economy Plus in Manage Booking. Lands Melbourne 07:45 Wed.

items.title: Free morning, pack, check out
items.notes: Breakfast at the hotel, a last walk to the river. Nothing to catch until 9:40.

items.title: Limited Express Hida Takayama → Nagoya
items.notes: ~2h30, reserved seat.

items.title: Nozomi Nagoya → Tokyo
items.notes: ~1h40, every 10 minutes.

items.title: Narita Express Tokyo → Narita T2
items.notes: Covered by the N’EX round-trip ticket bought on day 1.

culture.title: Takayama → Nagoya → Tokyo → home
culture.notes: No early start: the 9:40 Hida express, Shinkansen from Nagoya, Narita Express from Tokyo, at Narita by 3:30pm for the 7:20pm flight. QF80 check-in closes 18:20.

items.title: Land Melbourne T2: straight to SmartGate, collect bag, customs, Qantas domestic transfer desk, walk to T1
items.notes: 1h35 connection, protected because both flights are on the one booking; if QF80 is late Qantas rebooks you on a later Melbourne → Brisbane flight. No duty-free browsing: immigration, bag belt, customs, transfer desk, T1, gate. No time for a lounge.

items.title: QF1256 Melbourne → Brisbane
items.notes: QantasLink A220, 2h15. Confirmed.

items.title: AIRPARK shuttle to the car, lunch, drive to Gympie
items.notes: Two flights and a red-eye behind you: eat and have a proper coffee before the Bruce Highway. Home about 1:30pm.

confirmed.notes: Jetstar, Economy Classic Reward, 5,700 pts + A$43 taxes. Brisbane Terminal D (domestic). Separate booking from the Business reward, so not protected, but 6 hours of buffer. Bags not through-checked: collect at T2, re-check at T3.
Business Classic Reward. Domestic leg; check-in at Sydney T3. Same booking as QF49, so the connection is protected.

Paid fare, ¥92,570 (about A$857) for both sectors. Economy Sale fares are NOT eligible for Classic Upgrade Rewards, so a points upgrade to Business is off the table on this ticket. Economy Plus (extra legroom) is a seat product and may still be purchasable in Manage Booking with cash or points: worth trying. 30 kg checked allowance.

Same booking as QF80, so the 1h35 Melbourne connection is protected: if QF80 is late, Qantas moves you to a later Melbourne → Brisbane flight (roughly hourly) at no cost. Still, go straight to SmartGate on landing: 1h35 is enough, not generous.
Business Classic Reward. Seasonal Monday service (runs Sun/Mon/Wed/Fri, 2 Dec 2026 to late Mar 2027). Taxes paid: A$450.

legs.name: Home to Sydney, Mon 8 Feb
legs.notes: BOOKED: Jetstar JQ815 as a Classic Reward, landing 12:20 with six hours to spare. Being Jetstar it lands at T2 and the bag has to be collected and re-checked at T3, which the 6-hour buffer absorbs easily. Other options are kept below for the record.

options.label: Jetstar JQ815 Brisbane → Sydney (BOOKED)
options.notes: Economy Classic Reward. 20 kg bag should be included; confirm on the booking. Lands T2; walk 7 min to T3 and re-check the bag with Qantas.

options.label: Qantas Brisbane → Sydney, late morning
options.notes: Recommended. Park at BNE AIRPARK (A$109 for 8 days). With QF62 landing at BNE on the way home, this is the cheapest and simplest overall. 11:30 Queensland time → ~2:05pm Sydney time (AEDT): 4+ hours of buffer and lounge. Any QF flight landing before 3pm Sydney time works.

options.label: Qantas QF903 Sunshine Coast → Sydney
options.notes: 1 h from Gympie, parking ~A$90 for 8 days, no tolls. But if QF903 is cancelled the next Qantas flight lands after QF481 has gone, and the homeward flight lands at Brisbane, so you would need a A$55-85 shuttle back to the car. Times shown in Sydney time (AEDT).

options.label: Jetstar JQ787 Sunshine Coast → Sydney
options.notes: Cheapest fare, but arrives T2: collect bags, walk 7 min to T3, re-check, re-screen. No through-checking to Narita.

options.label: Qantas QF905 Sunshine Coast → Sydney, 7am (safest from MCY)
options.notes: Lowest risk if you insist on MCY: a whole day of fallback options. Long day in Sydney though (8+ hours in the lounge).

legs.name: Japan to home, Tue 16 Feb
legs.notes: BOOKED: QF80 + QF1256 as a paid Economy Sale fare. Background kept below. Big finding: the Brisbane flight (QF62) has no Premium Economy cabin at all, so “book economy and upgrade to PE” does not exist on it. The only Qantas Tokyo flight with PE is the 6:55am Haneda → Sydney. Realistic comfort upgrades: Economy Plus extra-legroom seats on the A330 (new from Sep 2026), or a Business Classic Reward if a seat appears. Points numbers marked “est.” are inferred from the Aug 2025 price rise; confirm on qantas.com when booking.

options.label: QF62 Narita → Brisbane, Economy Classic Reward
options.notes: No reward seats on 16 Feb when checked (Sep 2026). Keep an AwardFares alert running in case a batch is released; changing a booked reward costs a fee, so only switch for a Business seat. ~29,000 pts (est.) + ~A$120-170 taxes (Japan’s departure tax tripled to ¥3,000 from July 2026, so ex-Japan taxes are a little higher than older guides say). Add Economy Plus (extra legroom, ~19,500 pts or ~A$100-150 cash on similar routes) for comfort. Lands straight into Brisbane where the car is.

options.label: QF62 Narita → Brisbane, Business Classic Reward
options.notes: 82,100 pts (confirmed post-Aug-2025 price) + ~A$250-350 taxes. You have the points. Availability at Bronze in peak February is the only question; set alerts.

options.label: Jetstar JQ10 Narita → Brisbane, economy
options.notes: Cheapest points option (Jetstar table, ~24,000 pts est.; includes 20 kg bag). 787, no PE; you can bid for Jetstar Business with points + cash.

options.label: Jetstar JQ24 Osaka KIX → Brisbane (only if the trip is flipped to end in Osaka)
options.notes: Runs ~4x weekly; confirm Monday operates. Would let you do USJ on the last day and skip the Tokyo backtrack, at the cost of USJ on a Monday instead of Wednesday.

options.label: QF80 Narita → Melbourne 19:20 + QF1256 Melbourne → Brisbane 09:20 (BOOKED, cash Economy Sale)
options.notes: Booked as a paid Economy Sale fare (QF62 had no reward seats). Consequences: no points upgrade is possible on a Sale fare, so the 164k points stay in the bank for another trip; Economy Plus extra legroom may still be added in Manage Booking. 1h35 in Melbourne is protected because both flights are on one booking. Lands Brisbane 10:35 Wed, home early afternoon.

options.label: QF26 Haneda → Sydney, the only flight with Premium Economy
options.notes: 3-class A330 from Oct 2026. Economy ~36,200 pts est., PE ~74,000 pts est. Departs 6:55am (check-in from 4am, before trains run), so you would sleep at a Haneda hotel on the 15th and then still need SYD → Brisbane/Sunshine Coast. Only worth it if PE is the priority over everything else.

lounges.notes: Access comes from the Business cabin on your Classic Reward, not from status or passes. Entry opposite gates 4-5, up the escalator; Business Lounge is the left-hand door. Open until the last Qantas departure. Sydney’s First Lounge is in the international terminal (T1) and is not reachable from T3.

Airside, level 1. Covered by the Business ticket. Melbourne Airport lists a 10:15pm Monday close, but Qantas says lounges stay open until the last departure and Monday QF49 is a new service from Dec 2026: re-check the hours in January and be at the gate by 10:45pm regardless.

lounges.airport: Melbourne T2, First Lounge (level 3), Mon 8 Feb ~9pm-10:45pm
lounges.notes: Confirmed: your two passes are Qantas Money Titanium First Lounge invitations, which are valid at the Sydney, Melbourne and Los Angeles First Lounges when you are flying on a QF or JQ flight number. Use ONE here: escalator near gates 9-10 up to level 3, show the invitation in the Qantas app. Sit-down dining (the Neil Perry menu), spa if you book on arrival, showers. The second pass cannot be used on this trip (Narita has no Qantas First Lounge and you leave Sydney from the domestic terminal), so keep it for a later international departure. Third-party listings put closing at 10:15-11:15pm; be at the gate by 10:45pm. Invitations are cardholder-only and expire, so check the expiry date in the app now.

lounges.lounge: Qantas Club (via a Titanium card Qantas Club invitation)
lounges.notes: The Titanium card also gives two Qantas Club / International Business Lounge invitations a year, separate from the First Lounge ones. Qantas Club access is normally allowed when flying a Jetstar (JQ) domestic flight, so one of those invitations should open the Brisbane Qantas Club for an hour before JQ815. Check the invitation type in the app; it is a nice-to-have, not a plan.
Small terminal, four eateries, free wifi.

lounges.lounge: Economy: none. Business reward: JAL Sakura Lounge
lounges.notes: If you end up on the Business reward home, Qantas uses the JAL Sakura Lounge at Narita. In economy there is no lounge access; the 4F food court is good.
1h35 between landing and QF1256 is used up by immigration, bags, customs and the transfer. Skip the lounge.

list.name: Plan B: No skiing, Takayama hub, two nights out, free days

foodGuide.title: How to tell a place is happy to have you
foodGuide.body: Green lights: a menu or prices visible outside, a ticket machine (ramen, soba, gyudon), plastic food models, a photo or English menu, a listing on Tabelog, staff who call “irasshaimase” when the door opens, and any yakiniku, okonomiyaki, udon or soba shop. Nozawa, Tenma, Fukushima, Tsuruhashi and Narai are all used to visitors; you are not intruding.

foodGuide.title: When to bow out
foodGuide.body: A sign reading 一見さんお断り (ichigen-san okotowari, “first-timers not accepted”) or 会員制 (members only); a tiny “snack” bar with a hostess and no price list; a six-seat counter where every seat is a regular and the master does not look up. Being turned away is not an insult: a small bow, “sumimasen”, and try the next door. That system is mostly Kyoto tea-house culture anyway; Osaka standing bars welcome anyone who orders a drink.

foodGuide.title: Manners that matter more than language
foodGuide.body: Order a drink first, then food. The small dish that arrives unasked (otoshi) is a cover charge, not a mistake. One drink and a couple of plates, then move on when it is crowded; angle your body to make room at a standing bar. Cash out, no tipping ever. No photos of other customers or the counter without a nod from the master. “Oishii” and “gochisosama deshita” (thanks for the meal) on the way out go a long way.

foodGuide.title: Onsen and ryokan
foodGuide.body: Shoes off at the genkan, slippers off on tatami. Ryokan dinner is at a set time; be there. In the bathhouses: wash sitting down before you get in, no towel in the water, no swimwear, quiet, no phones. Tattoos: Nozawa’s village bathhouses are relaxed but cover-up stickers are cheap insurance if you have visible ink.

staysGuide.title: Why Booking.com looks empty
staysGuide.body: Booking.com carries maybe a third of Nozawa’s beds, and Japanese inns often list only twin rooms at a 2-person price, which makes a solo search show “sold out” or silly prices. Peak weeks (this is one) also get released to Japanese sites first.

staysGuide.title: Where the rooms actually are
staysGuide.body: 1. Rakuten Travel (travel.rakuten.com, English) and Jalan: search with 1 adult; they show single-occupancy plans with meals. 2. Email the inn directly in short simple English: dates, one person, one room, ask the price with breakfast. Most reply within a day. 3. Nozawa Holidays (nozawaholidays.com) manages a dozen lodges and will answer one email with everything that still has a solo room. 4. Stay Nozawa and nozawaonsen.ski run request forms that go to several properties at once.

staysGuide.title: What to ask for
staysGuide.body: “1 person, single occupancy, 11-16 Feb, private room, breakfast included if possible.” Expect a supplement of 20-30% over the per-person twin rate. Shared bathrooms are normal and fine: you will be in the village bathhouses anyway.

staysGuide.title: If it is truly full
staysGuide.body: Togari Onsen is 20 minutes by bus across the valley and much quieter and cheaper; sleep there and bus to Nozawa for skiing. Or switch base to Akakura Onsen (Myoko), where several ryokan take single bookings on Rakuten; only the Nagano end of the plan changes. Iiyama Station has very little lodging, so do not count on it.

points.notes: Update 13 Sep 2026: the flight home was booked as a paid Economy Sale fare, which cannot be upgraded with points (Sale classes E/N/O/Q are excluded from Classic Upgrade Rewards). Only the Jetstar feeder (5,700) has used points, so about 164k stay in the bank; Economy Plus on QF80 (~19,500 pts if offered) is the one remaining use on this trip. Prices confirmed post-5 Aug 2025: NRT→BNE Business 82,100; HND/NRT→SYD/MEL Business 98,400; short domestic (Zone 1) economy 9,200 + ~A$58. Economy Tokyo→Brisbane is estimated at ~29,000 (Zone 5) and Tokyo→Sydney/Melbourne ~36,200 (Zone 6); the exact cells were not visible from here, confirm on qantas.com. Bronze members are last in the upgrade queue and are typically only considered inside 24 h of departure, so treat any upgrade as a bonus, not a plan. Qantas’ Flight Reward Finder can be searched without logging in; AwardFares has a free Qantas search with alerts.

stays.name: Dormy Inn Premium Osaka Kitahama
stays.type: Business hotel with rooftop onsen bath
stays.distance: Kitahama: 20 min to Universal City by train; quiet business district by the river
stays.notes: Dormy Inns are the solo traveller’s friend: free late-night ramen, big bath, small clean rooms. Kitahama is calm and central.

stays.name: Toyoko Inn Osaka Umeda Nakatsu No.1
stays.distance: Nakatsu: 10 min walk to Nakazakicho, 20 min to USJ
stays.notes: Cheapest reliable option. Free breakfast (onigiri, miso soup). Book direct; the chain often has Feb availability when others are full.

stays.name: Hotel Universal Port Vita
stays.type: Official partner hotel, 10 min walk to USJ
stays.distance: Universal City: walk to the park gates, early-entry perks on some plans
stays.notes: Pay for convenience on USJ day only if the price is close. The Universal City area is a theme-park precinct, not a neighbourhood.

stays.name: Nozawa Peaks (guesthouse, book direct)
stays.type: Japanese-style guesthouse, private rooms, shared bath
stays.notes: Books direct for 2026-27 on its own site, English, used to solo guests. Ask for a single room rate.

stays.name: Lodge Nagano (Aussie-run lodge)
stays.distance: ~100 m from the slopes, short walk to the village centre
stays.notes: Affordable, easy English, solo-friendly. Also listed by Nozawa Holidays. You will be surrounded by Australians, which is the trade-off.

stays.name: Haus St. Anton (family-run pension hotel)
stays.type: 15-room boutique pension, private rooms with bath
stays.priceNote: Classic room from ~US$184; verify solo rate
stays.notes: Japanese family-run, European style, non-smoking, famous jam factory downstairs. Book direct on their English page. Top of the budget but the most Banff-like small hotel in the village.

stays.name: Nozawa Onsen Hotel
stays.notes: One of the few places with proper single rooms and its own onsen. Check Rakuten Travel and Jalan for single-occupancy plans; often cheaper than Booking.com.

stays.name: Lodge Matsuya / Lodge Nakajima (local family lodges)
stays.type: Minshuku-style lodge, private room, shared bath
stays.notes: Japanese-run, simple, warm, cheap. These are the ones that rarely show on Booking.com: use Rakuten/Jalan or email in simple English.

stays.name: Seisenso Inn (minshuku)
stays.type: Family-run minshuku, private room, shared bath
stays.distance: In the village, 5-10 min walk to Nagasaka gondola
stays.notes: Closest to the Banff-motel price point. Ask for a single tatami room with breakfast.

stays.name: Ginrei Lodge or Nozawa Springs Lodge (via Nozawa Holidays)
stays.notes: Nozawa Holidays manages a dozen lodges and will tell you in one email which ones still have a solo room for 11-16 Feb. Easiest single point of contact.

stays.name: Nozawa Dream Central (budget)
stays.notes: Confirm it is a private room, not a dorm, before booking.

stays.name: Mid-range ryokan with dinner and breakfast (Kawamotoya, Nozawa View Hotel Shimataka)
stays.notes: Planned as the budget placeholder until something is booked. A ryokan dinner is the local-cuisine experience you asked for and solves the solo-dinner question. Search these on Rakuten Travel with 1 adult.

stays.name: Togari Onsen pension (fallback, 20 min bus from Nozawa)
stays.distance: Across the valley from Nozawa; direct bus to Nozawa 20 min, Iiyama Station 30 min
stays.notes: Quiet little ski village with its own small resort. If Nozawa is truly full, sleep here and bus over for the Nozawa ski days. Fewer restaurants; more Japanese.

stays.name: Akakura Hotel (Myoko, accepts solo bookings)
stays.distance: Akakura Onsen village, walk to lifts
stays.notes: Explicitly takes reservations from one person. Also on Rakuten: Kounkaku (grand old ryokan), Kotobukiro, Hotel Takeda. Switching base changes only the Nagano end of the plan.

stays.name: Koyasan shukubo: Ekoin, Fukuchiin or Shojoshin-in
stays.notes: Book on the official Shukubo Association site (English). Ekoin is the most foreigner-friendly and runs the night tour; Fukuchiin has an onsen; Shojoshin-in sits right at the Okunoin entrance. Solo is normal. Night out no. 1.

stays.name: Takayama hub, 4 nights: Hotel Around Takayama, Tabino Hotel Hida Takayama or Hida Plaza Hotel
stays.type: Hotel with a big bath, by the station
stays.distance: Next to the station and the Nohi bus centre
stays.notes: One room for the whole second half: check in Friday, out Tuesday, and just don’t sleep here on Saturday night (Shirakawa-go). Send the suitcase here from Osaka (“for guest arriving 12 Feb”). Hotel Around Takayama is the newer stylish one; Tabino and Hida Plaza have proper onsen-style baths.

stays.name: Shirakawa-go gassho-zukuri farmhouse minshuku
stays.type: Thatched farmhouse, irori dinner and breakfast
stays.notes: Night out no. 2. Book through the Shirakawa-go Tourist Association reservation system (that guide explains it step by step). Around 40 places; ask for single occupancy. Not every house takes solo guests, so start early. No light-up event in Feb 2027, so no lottery.

food.where: Every meal; buy a bag from a village grandma’s shop to take home
food.why: The village’s signature food. Every family pickles its own; you will be offered it constantly.

food.where: Street stalls near Oyu and at Nagano Station
food.why: Grilled-then-steamed buns filled with nozawana, pumpkin or bean paste. The Nagano snack.

food.where: Main street, 100+ years in the Katagiri family
food.why: Hand-cut buckwheat noodles, cold zaru style with dipping sauce. Old shop, no fuss.

food.where: Any village izakaya
food.why: Nagano speciality, served with ginger and soy. Try it once.

food.where: Ogama, top of the village
food.why: Eggs slow-cooked in the 90°C spring. Locals cook their vegetables there too; it is the village kitchen.

food.where: Main street
food.why: Home-style teishoku that locals actually eat. Not a ski-bar.

food.where: Any counter with a hotplate in Fukushima or Tenma (avoid the Dotonbori queues)
food.why: Osaka’s home cooking. Sit at the teppan, order “buta-tama”, watch it made.

food.where: Izakaya alleys under the tracks at Tenma station
food.why: Beef tendon simmered in miso, and the deep-fried skewers Osaka is known for, in the part of town where office workers drink. No double dipping.

food.where: A stand with a queue of locals, not the ones with English menus
food.why: Octopus balls, Osaka’s thing. Eat them standing up, straight away.

food.where: Usami-tei Matsubaya (the shop that claims to have invented it, near Minami-Semba)
food.why: Udon in dashi with sweet fried tofu, Osaka’s soul food. Old shop, cheap.

food.where: Tsuruhashi station area
food.why: Osaka’s Korean neighbourhood; smoky yakiniku joints, nothing trendy about it. Good for a solo counter seat.

food.where: Shinsekai, a few doors from the famous Daruma
food.why: If you do go to Shinsekai, this is the locals’ pick over the tourist-famous Daruma. About ¥2,000 a head.

food.where: Fukumaru-dori, one Loop Line stop from Osaka Station
food.why: A workers’ dining street lined with small izakaya and bars; a good alternative base for dinner if the hotel is around Fukushima.

food.where: Ekibenya Matsuri, Tokyo Station
food.why: Regional lunch boxes to eat on the Shinkansen. Pick one from Nagano or Niigata.

food.where: Nagano Station area
food.why: Nagano is miso country. Warm you up after the Shinano train.

food.where: Super Nintendo World
food.why: The one touristy meal that is worth it: themed, and you are already inside.

food.where: Your temple, dinner and breakfast
food.why: Buddhist vegetarian cooking at its source. The sesame tofu is Koyasan’s own; buy a block from Hamadaya to take on the train.

food.where: A small grill off Sanmachi
food.why: Local beef cooked on a magnolia leaf over miso. The regional dish, not a tourist invention.

food.where: An old shop in the centre
food.why: Soy broth, thin curly noodles, what locals eat for lunch.

food.dish: Mitarashi dango at the morning market
food.where: Miyagawa market stalls
food.why: Soy-glazed, savoury not sweet here. Breakfast while you browse.

food.where: Your farmhouse
food.why: Char-grilled river fish, mountain vegetables, tofu, cooked over the sunken hearth. This is why you stay the night.

food.where: Watanabe or Kaba breweries, Hida Furukawa (15 min by train)
food.why: Two old breweries in a canal town nobody visits; ¥300 tastings, no queue.

food.where: A small sushi-ya near the station (ask the hotel)
food.why: Takayama is far from the sea, so the good places fly fish in daily and the locals know which ones; a counter seat is the solo traveller’s best dinner.

budget.label: Brisbane Airport AIRPARK, 9 days
budget.notes: A$99/week + A$10/day. Book online; sometimes cheaper than drive-up. MCY would be ~A$90 but needs a A$55-85 shuttle back from Brisbane on the way home.

budget.label: Travel insurance with snow-sports cover, 10 days
budget.notes: Must include skiing. Medicare does not cover Japan.

budget.label: Travel insurance, 10 days (no snow sports needed)
eSIM, 10 days data
budget.notes: Ubigi or Airalo; install before you leave.

budget.label: Onsen towels, ski socks, souvenirs, contingency
Suica top-ups (local trains, buses, vending machines)
USJ Express Pass 4 with Super Nintendo World entry (optional but recommended)
budget.notes: Nintendo-inclusive Express Pass 4 variants (e.g. “Mine Cart & Jaws”) were ~¥12,800 in 2026; Express Pass 7 ¥17,800-21,800. Names change every season: buy any Express Pass whose description includes “Super Nintendo World Area Entry” (ideally with Mario Kart and Mine-Cart Madness). Sells out on popular dates.

checklist.text: Check what your two lounge passes actually are: Qantas app → Complimentary Lounge Invitations → type (Titanium / Platinum One / General / Domestic) and expiry
checklist.notes: Only Titanium or Platinum One invitations open the Melbourne First Lounge. General/Domestic ones add nothing on this trip because the Business ticket already covers the Business lounges.

checklist.text: Keep a free AwardFares alert on QF62 NRT→BNE and QF80 NRT→MEL for 16 Feb 2027 (Business especially)
checklist.notes: Seats are released in batches. The paid Sale fare cannot be upgraded, but a Business Classic Reward could replace it if one appears and the Sale fare’s cancellation terms make it worthwhile (Sale fares are usually non-refundable, so probably not).

checklist.text: Book Nozawa Onsen accommodation for 11-16 Feb, 5 nights (long weekend; the village sells out)
checklist.notes: Email the minshuku directly for a single room, or Booking.com. Ask about single-occupancy pricing and whether dinner is included.

checklist.text: Book Osaka hotel for 9-11 Feb
checklist.notes: Toyoko Inn / Dormy Inn open bookings ~3-6 months ahead. Free cancellation where possible.

checklist.text: Book the flight home
checklist.notes: Done: QF80 + QF1256, Tue 16 Feb, paid Economy Sale fare, one booking. Add the booking reference to the Private vault, not here.

checklist.text: Book the Brisbane → Sydney feeder
Open Manage Booking for QF80 and try to add Economy Plus (extra legroom) with cash or points; pick seats on both flights
checklist.notes: Sale fares cannot be upgraded to Business with points, but the Economy Plus seat product is separate. If it is not offered on this fare, that is that.

checklist.text: Melbourne: 1h35 connection. SmartGate, bag, customs, domestic transfer desk, T1. Skip duty free.
Check the JQ815 booking shows a 20 kg checked bag (reward bookings include one, but the confirmation sometimes shows 0 kg); add a bag if not
Check in online for QF481 the day before (24 h out) so Sydney is bag-drop only
Book Brisbane AIRPARK online for 8-17 Feb
Buy USJ 1-Day Studio Pass + Express Pass 4 with Super Nintendo World entry for Wed 10 Feb (dates open 60 days ahead, so ~12 Dec 2026)
checklist.notes: Official USJ site or Klook (official partner; Klook lets you move the date within 90 days in the same price tier). Buy the day it opens. Create the USJ app account now: since Jan 2026 the app is mandatory for timed-entry tickets.

checklist.text: Travel insurance with the snow-sports add-on (and off-piste cover if you plan to ski Nozawa’s tree runs)
checklist.notes: Standard Australian policies exclude skiing. About A$80 for a week before the add-on. Buy it when you book the first non-refundable thing so cancellation cover starts. Medicare does not cover Japan.

checklist.text: Reserve Shinkansen and Shinano seats (smart-EX for Tokyo↔Osaka, JR East site for Hokuriku), opens 1 month before each travel date
checklist.notes: 9 Jan for the 9 Feb trains; 11 Jan for the 11 Feb trains; 16 Jan for the 16 Feb trains. Holiday Thursday trains fill.

checklist.text: Register on Visit Japan Web (immigration + customs QR)
checklist.notes: Australians get 90 days visa-free. Passport just needs to be valid for the stay, but check the expiry anyway.

checklist.text: Install eSIM (Ubigi ~US$14 for 10 GB/7 days, or Airalo) and set up Welcome Suica Mobile (iPhone) or plan to buy a physical Welcome Suica at Narita (Android)
checklist.notes: Suica works in Osaka (ICOCA area) and Nagano too. Google Wallet on non-Japanese Android phones generally cannot hold Suica; the physical Welcome Suica is cash top-up only and expires after 28 days, which is fine for this trip. Top up with Mastercard/Amex in Apple Wallet; some Visa cards fail.

checklist.text: Re-check Melbourne T2 lounge hours for Monday nights (Business Lounge and, if your passes qualify, First Lounge)
Tell your bank you are travelling; get ¥30,000-50,000 cash (or plan to withdraw at 7-Eleven ATMs on arrival)
checklist.notes: Ski villages and small restaurants are still cash-heavy.

checklist.text: Book ski rental online (village shop) for Fri 12, Sat 13, Mon 15 and Tue 16 morning with your boot size in cm; include ski wear if travelling light
checklist.notes: Big boot sizes run out in peak weeks. Pick a shop that opens by 7:45 so Friday is not lost.

checklist.text: Ski: thermals, mid-layer, gloves, goggles, beanie, buff, ski socks x3 (rent jacket/pants/skis/boots/helmet)
Onsen kit: small towel, plus a sense of humour about being naked with strangers
Carry-on for the plane: passport, printed e-ticket, USJ tickets, chargers, Type-A power adapter (Japan is 100 V, US-style plugs), snacks
USJ: through the gate, open the app, claim Super Nintendo World timed entry within seconds (or use the Express Pass slot)
Keep the N’EX round-trip ticket somewhere safe for the trip back to Narita

Tax-free shopping is now a refund at the airport (from Nov 2026): pay the 10% tax at the till, keep receipts and passport scans, and allow time at Narita to claim it back on Nintendo World or Osaka souvenirs
Open the Qantas app → Complimentary Lounge Invitations and confirm the Titanium First Lounge invitations show with an expiry after 8 Feb 2027
checklist.notes: They renew each card anniversary. If the current pair expires before February, the next pair will be issued on the anniversary; check which.

checklist.text: Ask the Nozawa lodging (when booking) whether they accept a courier parcel before arrival, and get their address in Japanese for the takkyubin slip
Reserve the Shinano seats Nagoya → Kiso-Fukushima and Shiojiri → Nagano for Thu 11 Feb, plus the local train times to and from Narai
checklist.notes: Holiday Thursday: reserved seats go. The local Chuo line runs roughly hourly, so match the connections when you book.

checklist.text: Buy simple strap-on crampons (or plan to buy at Workman/Don Quijote in Osaka) for the Togakushi snow walk
Saturday night: check Sunday’s weather. Powder dump = ski; anything else = Togakushi. Check the Alpico winter bus 70 timetable for the first bus and the last bus back
Return rental gear; settle the lodging bill in cash if they do not take cards
Narita T2 check-in closes 18:20 for QF80 (check in online the day before)
Plan B: book the Koyasan temple night on the Shukubo Association site (koyasan-shukubo.net), 11 Feb, 1 person with dinner and breakfast
Plan B: book a Shirakawa-go gassho farmhouse for 13 Feb through the Tourist Association reservation system (solo)
checklist.notes: The TravelClassroom guide walks through the form. Not all houses take single guests; try several.

checklist.text: Plan B: book the Takayama hub hotel for 4 nights, 12-16 Feb (one booking; you skip Saturday night there)
checklist.notes: Tell them a parcel arrives on the 11th for a guest checking in on the 12th.

checklist.text: Plan B: reserve the Nohi buses Takayama ↔ Shirakawa-go (13 and 14 Feb, late-morning services)
checklist.notes: Opens about a month ahead on nouhibus.co.jp.

checklist.text: Plan B: reserve the Nankai Limited Express Koya (11 Feb), Hida express Nagoya → Takayama (12 Feb) and Takayama → Nagoya (16 Feb, 9:40), and the Nozomi Nagoya → Tokyo (16 Feb)
Plan B: buy the Koyasan World Heritage Ticket at Nankai Namba on the morning of 11 Feb

places.notes: International. Business Lounge level 1, First Lounge level 3.

places.notes: Arrive 9 Feb, depart 15 Feb.

places.name: Tokyo Station
places.notes: N’EX arrives here; Shinkansen to Osaka and Nagano.

places.name: Universal Studios Japan
places.notes: Super Nintendo World. Universal City station is 5 min walk.

places.name: Tenma / Tenjinbashisuji
places.notes: Izakaya alleys and the long arcade.

places.name: Nakazakicho
places.notes: Old lanes, small cafes, 10 min from Umeda.

places.name: Takayama Station and bus centre (hub hotel)
Osaka hotel area (Kitahama / Nakatsu)
places.notes: Wherever the Osaka hotel ends up; move this pin.

places.name: Fukushima (Osaka) dining street

questions.question: Plan A (ski) or Plan B (no skiing)?
questions.why: Both use the flights already booked and the same Osaka and USJ days; they split on Thursday 11 Feb. Plan A: Nozawa Onsen for five nights, three ski days plus a rural Sunday, hinges on finding a solo room in a sold-out week. Plan B: Takayama as a four-night hub (one room, unpack once), with two nights out in great places (a temple at Koyasan, a farmhouse at Shirakawa-go), free afternoons and a free day, and no start before 9:30 except USJ, which the Express Pass makes optional. No dependence on Nozawa, and about A$500 cheaper because there are no lifts or rental. Lost workdays are identical. The plan switch at the top of the menu flips every page between them.
options: Plan A: ski trip (Nozawa Onsen)
Plan B: Takayama hub with Koyasan and Shirakawa-go nights out
Hybrid: Plan B with two of the Takayama nights swapped for Nozawa without skiing (onsen village, snow, food)
questions.recommendation: Decide by accommodation: if a Nozawa room lands by late October, Plan A. If not, Plan B is not a consolation prize; the Koyasan and Shirakawa-go nights are two of the best things you can do in Japan in winter, and every bed in it is easier to get.

questions.question: Ski base: Nozawa Onsen, Myoko (Akakura Onsen) or Hakuba?
questions.why: You said “south island”, which does not exist for skiing (Japan’s ski areas are on Hokkaido in the north and in the Nagano/Niigata mountains on the main island). Given Narita arrival + Osaka + a week, Nagano/Niigata is the only sensible region. Nozawa is the closest thing to Banff: a real village, walkable, hot springs, mountain rising straight off it, local food. It is also the most Australian of the villages and the busiest over the 11-14 Feb long weekend.
options: Nozawa Onsen (planned): Banff-like village, big mountain, local food, busiest and priciest of the three that weekend
Myoko / Akakura Onsen: quieter, cheaper, more Japanese, 13-16 m of snow, smaller mountain, fiddlier buses
Hakuba: biggest terrain and most Banff-like scale, but a sprawl of villages linked by buses and very international
questions.recommendation: Nozawa Onsen. If you decide “not hyped” matters more than terrain, switch to Myoko: the plan only changes at the Nagano end (Shinkansen to Joetsu-Myoko instead of Iiyama).

questions.question: Trip shape: Universal Studios first (Wednesday) or ski first and fly home from Osaka?
questions.why: Wed 10 Feb is the only calm weekday for USJ in the window (Thu 11 is a public holiday and the weekend follows, plus the tail of Lunar New Year travel). That forces the skiing onto the long weekend. The alternative is ski Wed-Fri (quieter slopes on Wed), then USJ on Mon 15 and fly Jetstar Osaka → Brisbane at 9:45pm that night, no Tokyo backtrack.
options: USJ Wed 10, ski Fri-Mon, fly QF62 Narita → Brisbane Mon 15 (planned)
Ski Wed-Fri, Osaka Sat-Mon, USJ Mon 15, Jetstar JQ24 Osaka → Brisbane Mon 15 night
questions.recommendation: Keep USJ on the Wednesday. Super Nintendo World on a crowded day is the thing most likely to spoil the trip, and Nozawa is big enough to absorb a weekend if you start at 8:30. Monday morning skiing is the bonus.
questions.answer: Ok sounds good. (And the flight home is now booked out of Narita, so ending in Osaka is no longer possible.)

questions.answer: Titanium credit card passes. One will be used in Melbourne; the other saved.

questions.question: Rent ski gear or bring your own?
questions.why: Rental in Nozawa is ~¥4,450-5,500 a day for skis, boots and poles, so 4 days is about A$165-200. Bringing skis means a 32 kg-allowance bag on the outbound (fine in Business) but hauling it through Tokyo Station, Osaka and two bus changes, plus the Shinkansen oversized-baggage rule.
options: Rent everything in the village, bring only boots if you love yours (planned)
Bring skis and boots
questions.recommendation: Rent. This trip has too many trains for a ski bag. Bring your own boots only if fit is a problem for you.
questions.answer: Rent in the village. The suitcase goes by courier and the itinerary has no room for a ski bag.

questions.question: Keep this repo public?
questions.why: The repo is public right now. That is why the app never writes booking references, ticket numbers or passport details to the repo (they live in the Private vault on your device). It is still safer to make the repo private since GitHub Pages works on private repos with a paid plan, or you can simply keep the rule: nothing sensitive in the plan text.
options: Keep public, keep sensitive details in the vault only (current)
Make the repo private (Settings → General → Danger zone). Pages on private repos needs GitHub Pro.
questions.recommendation: Keep public for now and use the vault; revisit if you want to store confirmation emails in the repo.
questions.answer: Keep public; sensitive details stay in the vault.

questions.question: Give up Sunday’s skiing for Togakushi and Zenko-ji, or fly home Tuesday to keep three full ski days?
questions.why: You asked for a rural day and said a ski day could go. Narai-juku is now built into Thursday’s travel day at no cost. Sunday is the worst ski day (long-weekend crowds), so it is the cheapest one to trade for Togakushi’s cedar avenue and Zenko-ji. That leaves Friday, Saturday and Monday morning on skis. Flying home Tuesday 16 instead would add a full quiet Monday on the slopes for about A$150 of lodging plus a day of leave.
options: Sunday rural day, Monday morning ski, fly Mon 15 (planned)
Sunday rural day and fly Tue 16 so Monday is a full ski day
Keep skiing Sunday; rural Japan is just the Narai stop on Thursday
questions.recommendation: As planned, with the powder-day escape hatch: if Sunday dawns dumping, ski and skip Togakushi.
questions.answer: Tue 16 is booked, so Monday is a full ski day and Sunday is the rural day, with the powder-day swap written into Sunday’s notes.

questions.question: Which rural stop, if you want a different one?
questions.why: Alternatives to Togakushi from Nozawa: Obuse (30 min from Nagano by Nagaden train, chestnut sweets, the Hokusai museum, sake brewery, old streets; easy and flat) or a dawn visit to Zenko-ji’s o-asaji morning service. Shirakawa-go’s farmhouses are the postcard but are 4+ hours each way from Nozawa and heavily touristed; not worth it on this trip. Matsumoto castle is a city.
options: Togakushi + Zenko-ji (planned): mountain shrine, cedars, soba, snow walk
Obuse + Zenko-ji: gentler, indoor-heavy, good if the weather is foul
Nothing beyond Narai
questions.recommendation: Togakushi, with Obuse as the bad-weather substitute.
questions.answer: Togakushi and Zenko-ji, with Obuse as the foul-weather substitute. Decide on the Saturday night.

questions.question: Rough budget ceiling?
questions.why: The plan currently totals roughly A$2,700-3,300 in cash on top of points, depending on Osaka hotel and the Express Pass. Knowing your ceiling decides whether to trade the ryokan half-board for a minshuku, and whether the Express Pass stays in.
options: Under A$2,500: minshuku, skip Express Pass, Jetstar home
A$2,500-3,500: as planned
Over A$3,500: ryokan with dinner every night, Business home if available
questions.recommendation: As planned. The Express Pass is the one “splurge” that buys back a whole day.
